one_month_reasoning: Scheduled in the window (to 2026-11-19): Q3 2026 results Thursday Oct 29 before the open with the rolled-forward 2027-2031 capital, financing and EPS outlook (call announcement [19]); expect Q3 near consensus $1.37 and 2026 guidance ($4.04-4.16) reaffirmed, while the plan adds capex (deck: $10B+ line of sight, funded ~40% equity [2]) so the reaction can go either way. The NSPM rate-freeze decision is not due until Jan-2027 [22]. Anthropic's IPO is now plausibly inside the window: Reuters (via TNW, 2026-09-06 [24]) had marketing from mid-October and listing before the Nov 3 midterms, while WSJ on Oct 20 still describes a draft S-1 [18], so pricing more likely lands in early-to-mid November. For XEL that is a flow event, not a fundamental one: utility holders are mostly income/low-volatility money, and the stock's month-to-month driver is the 10-year (5.12% on Oct 20, down from 5.21% on Oct 13 [23]). No directional edge: lognormal centred at ~$76.85 (slight carry) with ~5.8% one-month vol (19%/3.5 = 5.4% plus an earnings/plan-update bump); unchanged from round 1.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Discount kept at about today's level, a hair wider (0.90x vs 0.91x), not widened further. Persistent factors with evidence: (1) wildfire liability without a state shield in Colorado (2025 bill dropped [13]) and Texas (AG suit seeking damages and civil penalties [14][15]), with ~$80M of Smokehouse insurance left [1]; (2) Moody's negative outlooks at holdco (Baa1) and PSCo, FFO/debt planned flat at ~16% [1][2]; (3) the heaviest equity issuance in the group (69.7M forward shares, 11% of outstanding [3]) so per-share growth lags 11% rate-base growth; (4) regulatory lag: PSCo earns 7.22% vs 9.3% allowed on a 13-month average historical test year [2][21], NSPM proposes a 2027-28 base-rate freeze [22]. The extra 0.2 turn vs today reflects the Oct-29 plan roll-forward more likely adding than removing equity. Above-median EPS growth (~9%) argues against a wider discount.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$64 (-17%; ~13.4x my NTM EPS of $4.79 and ~14.3x today's NTM consensus $4.46; below every regulated peer except ES and ~7% under the $68.72 52-week low that XEL hit with the 10y near its 5.2-5.3% October peak) the market would be pricing NTM EPS near $4.30 at ~15x or an ES-like de-rating: most likely a new utility-caused wildfire with liability above insurance in CO/TX, a Texas AG outcome that blocks recovery, a Moody's holdco downgrade forcing block equity, an equity-heavy plan that cuts EPS growth to ~6%, or a regulatory reset (MN freeze without offset plus a sub-9% CO award), rather than rate- or IPO-flow-driven volatility. Re-underwrite there rather than average down; a flow- or rate-driven dip toward ~$70 (14.6x NTM) with the plan intact would instead be a buying opportunity.

reverse_dcf_check: Engine reverse DCF: the 17.0x P/E leg ($81.24) implies a 5.8% WACC with 3.5% terminal growth, i.e. a cost of equity of ~7.3% (0.51 x CoE + 0.49 x 4.27% = 5.8%), only ~2.1pt over the 5.12% 10-year; at my 6.1% WACC it needs earned returns above the 8.2-8.3% I model or growth above 3.5% after 2030. Plausible if (a) earned ROE converges toward allowed (9.3-9.6%) as the CO historical test year and MN freeze roll off, or (b) the data-centre pipeline keeps rate base compounding ~6-8% past 2030. The post-horizon risks (un-capped wildfire liability, affordability-driven ROE compression, AI-capex slowdown, organised opposition) cut against both, which is why I hold the multiple at 0.90x the group rather than the median.
dcf_check: The DCF ($63.74) is 22% below the P/E leg ($81.24). Argued, not zeroed: at a 6.1% WACC (cost of equity 7.75%) the unlevered return on rate base (~6.6-6.9%: 53.5% x 8.2% earned + 46.5% x ~4.5% debt cost) beats the WACC by only ~0.5-0.8pt, so the capex programme adds modest value; TV share is ~100% because FCFF is negative through the 2026-28 capex peak. The engine's reverse DCF says the 17x P/E needs a 5.8% WACC, i.e. a cost of equity of ~7.3% (2.1pt over a 5.12% 10y). I accept the supervisor's point that allowed ROEs (9.3-9.6%) exceed the cost of equity, which is why the DCF rose from $38 to $64 (lower CoE, holdco drag reconciled to the segment, base-plan capex), but I measure the spread on earned returns (OpCo 8.43% TTM, PSCo 7.22%), so a gap remains and the DCF leg keeps its band weight.

reasoning: Round 2 (skeptic). The supervisor's verified facts changed three of my inputs: (1) shares: the 10-Q schedules only the 27.3M 2025 forwards before the horizon, with the 42.5M 2026 forwards settling Dec-2027 to Dec-2028, so horizon shares are 658M (was 700M) and FY27/28 averages 653M/682M (was 678M/718M); (2) holdco drag: the deck's 'Holding company and other' segment was -$0.10/sh in H1 2026, so I recalibrated to -$138M in 2026, stepping up with holdco debt to -$200M/-$270M (was -$407M/-$492M interest-only); this also lowers the calibrated earned ROE to 8.33%, matching the deck's 8.43% TTM OpCo ROE; (3) regulatory lag is now built OpCo by OpCo from the CPUC 8-K (9.3% ROE, $157M vs $356M asked, 13-month average historical test year) and the NSPM freeze 8-K (base rates frozen 2027-28, ITC offset unquantified) instead of a flat 0.6pt haircut. Net: FY27 $4.53, FY28 $4.85, NTM $4.79 (round 1 $4.66), within 2% of consensus-equivalent $4.87. I rebuilt net debt with the front-loaded capex by year and a cash bridge ($49.1B, a bit above the supervisor's $48.5B because TTM CFO net of dividends is only $3.4B) and cut the cost of equity to 7.75% (10y 5.12% verified), so the DCF rose to $63.7 (from $38.5) and the blend to $77.74 (from $70.93). I keep two skeptic differences from the supervisor: 17.0x not 17.2x (the Oct-29 plan is more likely to add equity) and a -$125M probability-weighted Smokehouse/TX AG adjustment rather than -$80M. Bear evidence still stands: 10y up ~110bp y/y, Moody's negative outlooks, FFO/debt ~16%, $7B equity plus 40% equity on increments, PSCo 7.22% earned, no Colorado/Texas wildfire shield and ~$80M of insurance left. Anthropic/WSJ: no verified Anthropic load in Xcel territory (Abernathy in SPS is a Fluidstack site with a Google backstop and fully passed-through power per TeraWulf's 8-K; Anthropic's named sites are in Kentucky and Central Texas); the S-1's ~$450B of compute commitments, $111B with Google plus a >$160B TPU lease, is a general demand signal that runs through Google, Xcel's largest data-centre counterparty; its 'more organized' opposition risk factor matches the MN AG's challenge to the Google ESA and the CO affordability fight; tenant counterparty risk sits mostly on MN/CO tariff minimums, less so in SPS until its tariffs are filed. On IPO liquidity: a $2T listing is mainly funded by growth and tech holders and index rebalancing; XEL's holders are income and low-vol money, so any drain shows up as a short, flow-driven dip in AI-adjacent utilities rather than a re-rating. A dip toward ~$70 (14.6x NTM) with the plan intact would be a buying opportunity; below $64 is the thesis break. Distribution: scenarios $62 (26%) / $78 (51%) / $91 (23%) with 11-13% within-scenario vol (total ~18%, near the 19% realised); median ~$76.7 (spot: price beats blends as a forecast), mean ~$76.8. Engine scenario values (bear $56.9, bull $95.3) are wider because the DCF leg moves with the deltas. Research limits: SEC refused scripted fetches (filings read through WebFetch), and no beta feed was available, so the equity premium is judgment.
